newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 17.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's edition of The Wall Street Journal:
- Technology stocks were hit by another round of heavy selling.
- Providian is seeking a buyer for its big but underperforming insurance operations.
- Boeing faces the daunting task of meshing McDonnell Douglas with its own operations after announcing plans to acquire its rival for about $14 billion.
- Credit card issuers are launching a major lobbying effort to toughen federal bankruptcy laws as part of a drive to get more money back from consumers with big debt problems.
- Industrial output rose 0.9 percent in November.

- The lead trade group for Health Maintenance Organizations is expected to endorse curbs on the use of so-called gag clauses and take other steps aimed at improving relations with physicians and patients.
- Safeway said it signed a definitive, $1.57 billion pact to acquire Vons Cos after revising its offer to offset the falling price of Safeway's shares.
- Natural gas futures rose to records on the Nymex as an Arctic blast was expected to hit much of the country this week combined with low inventories.
- The FAA is considering an order to limit the size of payloads on key aircraft flown by Federal Express and other major air-freight carriers.
- Former Daiwa Bank bond trader Toshihide Iguchi was sentenced by a federal judge to four years in prison.
- TWA appointed three directors as interim managers after searching in vain for two months for a president and CEO to succeed Jeffrey Erickson.
- Cable Giant Tele-Communications Inc said it will merge its telephone service operations into a single unit.
- Ronald Perelman's Andrews Group sweetened its bid for Toy Biz for a second time in three weeks.
- AT&T brought in former Citibank executive Richard Srednicki to help turn around its credit card division.
- Wall Street reacted enthusiastically to Boeing Co's planned merger with McDonnell Douglas, pushing shares of both higher.
- Bond prices fell across the board as early weakness extended into a broader sell-off in afternoon trading.
